articles.title: India Eyes Venezuelan Oil Fields as Caracas Becomes Its Fourth-Largest Crude Supplier
articles.excerpt: Petroleum minister tells Caracas that Indian companies want upstream exploration. Imports surged 51 percent in a single month as the Hormuz crisis forces a historic rewrite of India's oil map.

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Xi Jinping Heads to Pyongyang on Monday. India Is Reading the Room.
articles.excerpt: China's president will make his first visit to North Korea in seven years. Kim Jong Un has been flexing nuclear muscle all week. For New Delhi, the summit reshapes the security math across Asia.
articles.image_caption: Chinese President Xi Jinping, who heads to Pyongyang on Monday for his first North Korea visit in seven years
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran Fired Missiles Over Residential Kuwait Again. India Has 52,000 Reasons to Worry.
articles.excerpt: Seven ballistic missiles targeted Kuwait and Bahrain on Saturday. More than 52,000 Indians have already been evacuated from the Gulf since March. The flights keep getting cancelled.
articles.image_caption: A U.S. Navy patrol ship transits the Strait of Hormuz, the waterway at the centre of the Iran-US conflict

articles.title: Shivakumar Takes Over as Karnataka CM. Within 48 Hours, a Minister Has Already Quit.
articles.excerpt: DK Shivakumar's swearing-in marks a major Congress transition in Karnataka, but a portfolio dispute has already triggered the first cabinet resignation — testing the new government before it could settle in.
articles.image_caption: DK Shivakumar, the newly sworn-in Chief Minister of Karnataka
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 535 Farmers Dead from Pesticide Exposure in Two Years. Rajasthan's Assembly Tabled the Numbers.

articles.image_caption: Farmers working in agricultural fields in rural Rajasthan
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Cook's Negligence, a Hotel with No Fire Clearance, and 21 Dead in Delhi
articles.excerpt: The Malviya Nagar fire has killed 21 people — 13 of them foreign nationals — and exposed a city-wide failure of safety enforcement in Delhi's budget hospitality sector.
articles.image_caption: Firefighters respond to a building fire in an urban area
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Monsoon Just Reached Maharashtra on Schedule. Kerala's Late Start Did Not Slow It Down.
articles.excerpt: The southwest monsoon entered Maharashtra on Friday, despite arriving in Kerala three days late. IMD says conditions favour rapid advancement across central India this week.
articles.image_caption: Monsoon rain sweeps across an Indian landscape — the southwest monsoon reached Maharashtra on schedule this week (CC BY)
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Tells Bangladesh to Verify 2,860 Nationals for Deportation. Bangladesh Says India Is Pushing People Across the Border.
articles.excerpt: A bilateral mechanism exists on paper. In practice, 2,860 verification requests sit unanswered while both sides trade accusations across a 4,000-kilometre frontier.
articles.image_caption: BSF personnel guarding the India-Bangladesh border in Sylhet, one of the longest land frontiers in the world

articles.title: India and Nepal Launch Cross-Border UPI Payments. Millions of Migrant Workers Stand to Benefit.
articles.excerpt: Jaishankar hands over 84 post-earthquake reconstruction projects and launches a digital payment corridor that could reshape how Nepal's workers in India send money home.

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Will Surpass Nehru on Tuesday as India's Longest-Serving Elected Prime Minister
articles.excerpt: On June 10, Modi will complete 4,399 consecutive days in office, overtaking the record held by Jawaharlal Nehru since 1964. The milestone caps a political journey from Gujarat's chief minister's chair to three consecutive national mandates.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressing media in New Delhi
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Convenes Economic War Room as West Asia Crisis Tests India's 7.7% Growth Story
articles.excerpt: The PM-Economic Advisory Council meeting reviewed energy shock preparedness, trade route disruptions and reform blueprints — a day after GDP data confirmed India as the world's fastest-growing major economy
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi in an official portrait
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Paying Russia a 425% Higher Premium for Oil. It Is Buying More Anyway.
articles.excerpt: Russia's share of India's crude imports jumped to an 11-month high of 38 per cent in April as the West Asia crisis forced New Delhi to scramble for every barrel it could find
articles.image_caption: The Jamnagar Refinery in Gujarat, the world's largest oil refining complex — India's crude imports from Russia hit a 37.7 per cent share in April 2026 (Wikimedia Commons)

articles.title: UPI Just Had Its Biggest Month Ever. India Processed ₹29.9 Lakh Crore in May.
articles.excerpt: A record 23.2 billion transactions — nearly 740 million a day — were powered by summer travel, IPL spending and the quiet expansion of digital payments into every corner of Indian life
articles.image_caption: The UPI logo — India's digital payment system processed a record ₹29.9 lakh crore across 23.2 billion transactions in May 2026 (Wikimedia Commons)

articles.title: The Pentagon Just Called India a 'Critical Anchor.' Then It Offered to Co-Produce Javelin Missiles.
articles.excerpt: At the Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore, US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth described India as essential to Indo-Pacific stability and confirmed joint production of Javelin anti-tank guided munitions — a level of defence-industrial integration Washington has reserved for its closest allies.
articles.image_caption: US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth at the Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Launches E85 Fuel at ₹20 Below Petrol. The Flex-Fuel Era Has Begun.
articles.excerpt: The oil minister unveiled 85-percent-ethanol fuel on World Environment Day, with Maruti Suzuki, Hero MotoCorp and Toyota already rolling out compatible vehicles. The timing, with crude above $100 and the Strait of Hormuz partially closed, is not accidental.
articles.image_caption: Union Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri, who launched E85 fuel in New Delhi
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and Australia Just Widened Their Defence Partnership. Maritime Security Is the Centrepiece.
articles.excerpt: Rajnath Singh and Australian counterpart Richard Marles agreed to expand cooperation in maritime security, cybersecurity and emerging technologies — a step Australia's government described by calling India a 'top-tier security partner.'
articles.image_caption: Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, who met his Australian counterpart in New Delhi

articles.title: Putin Says Any Sanctions Threat Against India Would 'Boomerang Immediately' Under Modi
articles.excerpt: At the St Petersburg Economic Forum, the Russian president backed India's strategic autonomy, projected $100 billion bilateral trade, and dismissed American pressure on New Delhi as 'detrimental' to international relations.

articles.title: Trump Says an Iran Deal Is 'Largely Negotiated.' India Is Watching the Strait.
articles.excerpt: A proposed 60-day ceasefire extension and reopening of the Strait of Hormuz would ease the energy shock that has battered India's economy for three months. But the nuclear question remains unresolved.

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump's Own Party Just Voted to End His War and Fund Ukraine. The Cracks Are Widening.
articles.excerpt: In a single week, House Republicans defied the president on Iran, Ukraine, his ballroom, and a $1.8 billion settlement fund. For Indian Americans watching immigration and trade policy, the intra-party revolt may reshape what gets done before November.

articles.title: The US Just Proposed a 12.5% Tariff on India. The Justification: Forced Labour in the Supply Chain.

articles.title: The RBI Just Held Rates for the Third Straight Meeting. It Is Betting the War Will End Before Inflation Arrives.

articles.title: The World's Oil Cushion Is Almost Gone. Exxon Just Warned of $150 Crude.

articles.title: India’s Monsoon Has Arrived. The Forecast Says It May Not Be Enough.

articles.title: Five Astronauts Just Sheltered for Evacuation on the Space Station. The Leak Is Getting Worse.

articles.title: ICE Just Found 10,000 Cases of OPT Fraud. A Legal Petition Could Kill the Program Entirely.
articles.excerpt: The Optional Practical Training programme is how most Indian graduates stay in the US after college. A conservative legal foundation has petitioned DHS to shut it down — and the Trump administration may be listening.

articles.title: India Is Quietly Rebuilding Its Oil Map. Venezuela Just Became Its Fourth-Largest Supplier.
articles.excerpt: As Hormuz stays shut, Indian refiners are locking in crude from Latin America and Africa. The shift is starting to look less like a stopgap and more like a structural overhaul of how India buys energy.

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Just Struck Iranian Radar Sites After Shooting Down Four Drones Over Hormuz. India's Oil Lifeline Is in the Crossfire.
articles.excerpt: Saturday's exchange marks the sharpest flare-up since the April ceasefire. With Brent crude at $93 and India's LPG under-recovery at ₹700 per cylinder, every escalation lands directly on Indian household budgets.
articles.image_caption: An oil tanker at sea — the Strait of Hormuz normally carries a fifth of global oil traffic
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Doubled the Spending Power of Its Military Commanders
articles.excerpt: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's new procurement framework gives field commanders authority over ₹1.25 lakh crore in annual purchases — and cuts the ministry out of 80-90% of contracts.
articles.image_caption: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh at the DFPDS-2026 release in New Delhi
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora defence-tech entrepreneurs and investors in dual-use technologies gain a wider entry point as India doubles R&D procurement powers, accelerates approval cycles, and explicitly prioritises indigenous suppliers over foreign OEMs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Buyers Once Made Up 70 Percent of Sales in North Dallas. The H-1B Crackdown Changed That Overnight.
articles.excerpt: Home prices in Collin County have fallen nearly 9 percent year-over-year. Over 100 luxury homes sit unsold. The suburbs that Indian tech workers built are learning what happens when they leave.
articles.image_caption: The Dallas-Fort Worth metro area attracted more corporate relocations than any other US city
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Federal Judge Just Struck Down Trump's Immigration Freeze on 39 Countries. The Ruling Is 135 Pages Long.
articles.excerpt: The court found that USCIS acted without legal authority and was driven by anti-immigrant animus, not national security. Indians on pending applications should take note.
articles.image_caption: A federal courthouse in Providence, Rhode Island, where the ruling was issued
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Immigrants Built 96 Billion-Dollar Startups in America. The Combined Value Exceeds Germany's Stock Market.
articles.excerpt: A new NFAP study finds that 59 percent of US unicorns have at least one immigrant founder. India leads all 76 source countries by a wide margin.
articles.image_caption: Silicon Valley, the epicenter of America's billion-dollar startup ecosystem
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The WMO Says This Could Be the Strongest El Niño on Record. India's Food Supply Is in the Path.
articles.excerpt: An 80 per cent probability of El Niño by August, 90 per cent through November, and sea surface temperatures 6°C above average. The monsoon is already late.
articles.image_caption: Cracked earth in a drought-hit region — the WMO warns 2026 could bring the strongest El Niño ever recorded
articles.nri_angle: El Niño threatens higher food prices in India, potential rice and wheat export bans that affect diaspora food imports, and a harder macroeconomic environment that complicates the RBI's rate decisions — all directly impacting remittance value and NRI family budgets back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Just Added 172,000 Jobs. A Fed Rate Hike Is Now the Base Case. Here Is What That Means for NRIs.
articles.excerpt: May payrolls crushed forecasts, the unemployment rate held at 4.3 per cent, and the probability of a December rate hike jumped to 70 per cent. The dollar-rupee equation just shifted.
articles.image_caption: The US Federal Reserve building in Washington — markets now see a 70 per cent chance of a rate hike by December
articles.nri_angle: A Fed rate hike strengthens the dollar and pressures the rupee, directly affecting remittance values. Strong job growth supports H-1B sponsorship but the sectors hiring fastest are not tech — while long-term unemployment is rising among younger, educated workers who overlap with H-1B and OPT visa holders.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
